messages:
sam: Quick flag — our canary rollout for v2-routing is showing ~3x p95 on conv workloads in staging this morning. Observed during peak replay window.

alex: Saw that too. Metrics point to a high rate of KV cache misses on the small canary pool (single shard), cold startup effects.

neha: That aligns with traces — lots of 'kv_lookup miss' at token 0. Canary pool size + short TTLs are killing effective cache hit rate.

lee: Is this a perf-only problem or do we expect semantic drift if we change cache behavior for canaries?

sam: Good Q. If we change cache policy for canary traffic (e.g. no prefix caching), outputs may diverge slightly. But we need to trade off too-high tail latency vs comparison fidelity.

neha: Proposal: 1) Disable prefix/KV caching for canary requests, 2) run parallel async warmup tasks that prefill the canary KV shards using a small set of synthetic prefixes, 3) ramp canary traffic slower and add an automatic fallback trigger at p95>450ms or error_rate>0.7%.

alex: I like the warmup idea. Implementation detail: warmups should be run from the same region and same GPU type to reproduce kernel caches. Also keep warmups under a low-priority queue so they don't steal capacity.

lee: Concern: disabling prefix caching changes throughput and could mask correctness regressions. Suggest we keep a small mirrored stream with full-cached behavior for output comparison (A/B mirror) while production traffic goes to the no-cache canary.

neha: Yep — mirror approach for diffs, no-cache for latency characteristics. Mirror traffic is sampling-only and not in the critical path.

sam: Ops implications: we need two control knobs in rollout config: canary_cache_policy and canary_warmup (cron + sample prefixes). Also a fallback policy that can route traffic to the previous stable model variant or to a quantized cheaper variant if cost is a concern.

alex: Draft rollout snippet for config:

```yaml
rollout:
  name: v2-routing-canary
  stages:
    - percent: 1
      duration: 30m
      cache_policy: NO_PREFIX_CACHE
      warmup: enabled
    - percent: 5
      duration: 1h
      cache_policy: NO_PREFIX_CACHE
      warmup: enabled
  fallback:
    triggers:
      - metric: p95_latency_ms
        threshold: 450
      - metric: error_rate_pct
        threshold: 0.7
    action: revert_to: v1-routing
    grace_period: 120s
```

lee: Two extra asks: (a) define exact semantic difference between NO_PREFIX_CACHE and FULL_CACHE in docs, (b) surface the warmup progress and keystats in console (prefill hit rate, last_warmup_ts).

neha: On (b) — I can add telemetry events: canary_warmup.started/finished, warmup.prefill_hits, warmup.prefill_misses. Those will feed into Console and into automatic fallback evaluation.

deploy-bot: deploy-checks: canary cluster size=1 -> warn: cold-KV risk.

sam: Ops-bot: please add an automated job to run warmup prefills when canary cluster spins up; keep rate limit 5qps and use the synthetic prefix set shared in docs.

ops-bot: scheduled job created: /jobs/canary-warmup/v2-routing (5qps, retries=2).

alex: One more decision point — do we accept that the canary is "latency-faithful but cache-unfaithful" and rely on mirrored outputs for correctness, or do we invest in pre-warming to make it both faithful and low-latency? The latter costs GPU cycles.

neha: Tradeoff doc: if customer-facing latency is priority for rollout gating, then prefer NO_PREFIX_CACHE + warmup. If output fidelity for semantic regression detection is priority, keep FULL_CACHE and accept slower p95 but stricter regression signals. We'll recommend default: NO_PREFIX_CACHE + mirror for diffs.

sam: Consensus in thread: proceed with neha's proposal, add mirror channel for diffs, implement warmup job, and enforce fallback triggers in rollout engine. I'll open a follow-up RFC with exact config schema and SLO numbers.

lee: :thumbsup: Please add a note about observability dashboards and an alert runbook reference.

neha: I will draft the RFC and runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-cache-warmup> and ping infra for perf budget approval.

sam: Thanks all — filing RFC and scheduling a 30m sync tomorrow to sign off on config details.

alex: FYI — captured perf traces at <https://perf.redwood/sessions/76421>.

deploy-bot: deployment-note: canary rollout halted automatically at 1764207032 due to p95 breach (simulated).

sam: Good — fallback exercised as intended in staging. We'll validate warmup reduces regression.
